FIX SCOPE: this is not one site. Swept R/ for the same pattern and found three places that densify the m-by-p sparse frame.

  R/measurement.R:494              .additive_frame_signature       weights = as.matrix(frame$weights)
  R/measurement.R:511              .measurement_frame_from_additive weights <- as.matrix(frame$weights)
  R/measurement-decomposition.R:76 (frame decomposition)            weights <- as.matrix(frame$weights)

All three take the same object, so all three cost 18.6 GiB at p = 50000. Note that .measurement_frame_from_additive triggers it twice - once directly at :511 and once via .additive_frame_signature at :513.

Only the first is on the plan path that fails today, which is why the reproduction lands there. The other two sit in the measurement-form and decomposition subsystems, so they are latent rather than currently firing - but they are the same defect and they live in exactly the subsystem that is supposed to reach brain scale later.

Checked and CLEAN, no action needed:
- R/metric.R:608-621 (.frame_metric_node) handles the sparse case properly via Matrix::summary and only falls back to as.numeric for a genuinely non-sparse row. Correct as written.
- The as.matrix() calls in measurement-kernel.R:137/366/585, measurement-result.R:100/120/414/468/803 and evidence-task.R:620/651 are all on query$operator, which is q-by-q on the experimental side. q is the condition count, so those are small and fine.
- support-index.R:158/208 are expand.grid offsets, unrelated.

So the fix is: canonicalize once (see my corrected-fix note) and route all three sites through it, rather than patching only the one that currently fails.
